submission.justification: Module-D1 collects the most light (38 PE/MeV at 20% coverage), but 30% of D1 modules failed thermal cycling because the thin light-guide bond cracks. The limit is 5%, and modules cannot be reached once the cryostat is filled, so D1 is ruled out. Of the two robust designs, D2 (2% failures) collects much more light than D3 (0.5% failures): 27 vs 18 PE/MeV at 20% coverage. Light collection rises with coverage, so I chose the maximum allowed, 30%. The cabling feedthroughs support up to 30% coverage. Using the 2025 coverage^0.8 scaling, D2 at 30% should give about 27 × 1.5^0.8 ≈ 37 PE/MeV. This is an estimate from that scaling rule. I did not run a new simulation (no simulation tool was available), and the 2025 results were only for 20% coverage.

requirements.evidence: D2 collects the most light of the robust designs: 27 vs 18 PE/MeV for D3 at 20% (2025 simulation). At the maximum 30% coverage the coverage^0.8 scaling gives about 37 PE/MeV. This is an estimate, not a new simulation.
